Glossary

Terms on this level first.

Resident blocks per SM

An SM holds as many copies of a block as its tightest resource allows. The resources are four: warp slots, the register file, shared memory, and the block table, each explained below. Those blocks' warps fill the SM's warp slots, and the filled fraction is the occupancy.

SM limits, this GPU

What is limited, and why illustrative

An SM runs blocks. Before a block can start on an SM, four things must have room for it: warp slots, registers, shared memory, and the block table. If any one of them is full, the block waits for another SM or for a block to finish.

SM resources occupancy calculator

Kernel
Registers per thread come from the compiler (ptxas -v); 32 is an assumption for both presets. Register use is rounded up to the allocation unit per warp, as the hardware does.
The four resources, filled by this kernel's blocks
warp slots / threads registers shared memory block table unused room the limit that binds

The calculator counts whole blocks against the four budgets, as the lesson does. NVIDIA's occupancy calculator adds what it leaves out: a per-block shared-memory reservation and allocation granularity, registers allocated per partition (a block's warps rounded up to the partition count, each partition's share filled separately), launch bounds and clusters.
